title: Boebert loses Colorado's 4th District to Democrat Laubacher
h1: Rep. Lauren Boebert has lost Colorado's 4th Congressional District to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, the Associated Press says
description: The AP called Colorado's 4th Congressional District for Democrat Eileen Laubacher on November 13, 2026. She led Rep. Lauren Boebert by 3,525 votes.
standfirst: The call came 10 days after Election Day in the district considered the most Republican in Colorado. Boebert has not conceded, and the margin is too wide for an automatic recount.
keywords: Lauren Boebert loses, Eileen Laubacher, Colorado 4th Congressional District 2026, CO-4 results, AP race call, Colorado recount rules, Jeff Hurd
takeaways: The AP called the race at 12:53 p.m. on Friday, November 13, with Laubacher at 48.8% and Boebert at 47.9%.
Laubacher led by 3,525 votes out of just under 385,000. An automatic recount needs a margin of 0.5% or less.
Colorado will send seven Democrats and one Republican, Rep. Jeff Hurd, to the U.S. House next year.
body: Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert has lost her seat in Colorado's 4th Congressional District to Democrat Eileen Laubacher. The Associated Press called the race at 12:53 p.m. on Friday, November 13, 10 days after the election, The Colorado Sun reported.

Laubacher had 48.8% of the vote to Boebert's 47.9%, with Libertarian Douglas Mangeris at 3.3%. Her lead was 3,525 votes out of just under 385,000 counted, according to Colorado Politics. The count ran long because of late military and overseas ballots and ballots with signature problems that voters can fix after Election Day, the Sun said.

The district covers the Eastern Plains, Douglas County and Loveland, and the Sun describes it as the most favorable to Republicans in the state. Boebert won it by 11.6 percentage points in 2024. President Trump carried it that year by just over 18 points, according to figures from The Downballot cited in a separate Sun analysis. Laubacher is only the second Democrat to win the seat since 1973.

Laubacher, 58, lives in Highlands Ranch. She is a retired Navy rear admiral who served 34 years, and this was her first run for office. She raised $13.7 million through mid-October, compared with $1.2 million for Boebert, the Sun reported.
"This campaign was never about party labels. It was about putting people first," Laubacher said, according to Colorado Politics.

Not automatically. State law triggers one only when the margin is 0.5% or less, and this one was 0.91%, Colorado Politics reported. Any candidate can ask for a recount but has to pay for it. Boebert has not conceded. She told reporters in Washington she did not expect to pay for a recount, though a fundraising email said her legal team was preparing for one.

Democrats also unseated Republican Reps. Gabe Evans in the 8th District and Jeff Crank in the 5th. That leaves Rep. Jeff Hurd of the 3rd District as the only Republican in Colorado's eight-member House delegation when new members are sworn in early next year. Boebert, who served six years in Congress, said before the call that she would not seek a rematch if she lost.
